identity.title: Probing the jet base of the blazar PKS 1830-211 from the chromatic variability of its lensed images. Serendipitous ALMA observations of a strong gamma-ray flare

paper_type_evidence.quote: The observations are part of an ALMA Early Science Cycle 0 project for the spectral study of absorption lines in the $z$=0.89 lensing galaxy toward PKS 1830$-$211
We present multi-epoch and multi-frequency ALMA Early Science Cycle 0 submm continuum data of the lensed blazar PKS 1830$-$211

evidence.quote: The blazar is located at a redshift of $z$=2.507$\pm$0.002 ((cite: lid99)) and is lensed by a foreground $z$=0.89 galaxy ((cite: wik96))
The blazar is located at a redshift of $z$=2.507$\pm$0.002 ((cite: lid99)) and is lensed by a foreground $z$=0.89 galaxy ((cite: wik96))

question.value: Can the chromatic, time-variable flux ratio of the two lensed images of PKS 1830-211 during a gamma-ray flare constrain the jet structure and physics near the jet base (core-shift, plasmon ejection)?

evidence.quote: We show that such observations can help constrain the physics of plasmon ejection in regions very close to (if not at) the base of the collimation region in the jet.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00405.S .
The observations were taken in spectral mode at frequencies around 100 GHz (B3), 250 GHz (B6), 290 GHz (B7), and 300 GHz (B7)

evidence.quote: For each tuning, four different 1.875 GHz-wide spectral windows were set, each counting 3840 channels separated by 0.488 kHz.

evidence.quote: The array configuration resulted in a synthesized beam of $\sim$ $2''$ in B3, and $\sim$ $0.5''$ in B6 and B7.
Data were taken on 9–11 April (B6 and B7), 22–23 May (B3, B6, and B7), 4 June (B3 and B7), and 15 June 2012 (B3 and B6)

analysis_steps.goal: Measure NE flux and NE/SW flux ratio per epoch and spectral window

method.value: Visibility model-fitting of two point sources (NE, SW), fitting f_NE and ratio R, after removing line channels; repeated after phase self-calibration

evidence.quote: The continuum emission of the blazar images was thus modelled as two point sources (NE and SW).
we have fitted the values $f_{NE}$, the flux density of the NE image, and $\Re$=$f_{NE}$/$f_{SW}$, their flux-density ratio.
the remaining number of line-free channels was always large (typically $>$2000).

evidence.quote: we checked that their contribution becomes negligible for the ALMA observations.

fitting.value: Uncertainties from covariance matrix at chi2 minimum, scaled so reduced chi2 = 1

evidence.quote: The parameter uncertainties were derived from their covariance matrix, computed at the $\chi^ 2$ minimum, and scaled so that the reduced $\chi^2$ equals unity.

analysis_steps.goal: Test micro/milli-lensing as cause of variability

method.value: Compare Einstein radius with core size and timescales

evidence.quote: we get a typical Einstein radius $\theta_E = 1.7$ $\mu$as.

assumptions.value: Core size scales as nu^-1 for conical jet, from 0.5 mas at 43 GHz

evidence.quote: In the case of a conical jet, the size of the core emission should scale roughly as $\propto \nu^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit plasmon-in-jet model (conical and concave) to flux ratios vs time and frequency

method.value: Simplified Marscher jet model with plasmon over-density; flux ratio computed using 27-day lens delay; least-squares minimization against observed ratios

evidence.quote: A direct comparison between the observed ratios and the model predictions allows us to constrain the defining parameters of the jet model by means of least-squares minimization.

key_parameters.value: Fixed: theta = 3 deg, delay = 27 days, nu0 = 100 GHz, tau = 1

evidence.quote: Opacity, $\tau_{\nu 0}$, at $\nu_0$ and $R_0$

assumptions.value: Very narrow jet tube; plasmon keeps width and contrast; B scaled to keep particle/field energy ratio

evidence.quote: we assume that the jet tube (where the plasma is confined) is very narrow, so that $r \ll R$ for all $R$.

fitting.value: Parameter ranges reported with max 20% chi2 increase over minimum; 8 (conical) or 9 (concave) parameters

evidence.quote: report the range of values that match the data with a similar quality (maximum increase in the $\chi^ 2$ of 20% with respect to the minimum value)

validation.value: Compared model flux ratios and spectrum with data; conical model fails to reproduce spectrum (alpha=0.7)

evidence.quote: the conical-jet model is clearly unable to reproduce the optically-thin spectrum seen in the data ($\alpha$=0.7)

evidence.quote: From our jet models, both conical and concave, we estimate a distance of 0.3–0.5 pc between the cores at 100 GHz and 300 GHz.

findings_qualitative.value: Flux-ratio variations are chromatic and imply intrinsic jet structure (core-shift); micro/milli-lensing is excluded by timescale.

evidence.quote: We rule out the possibility of micro- and milli-lensing, based on the timescale of the variability.

findings_qualitative.value: Submm and gamma-ray flares are co-spatial near the jet base.

evidence.quote: we suggest that both flares are co-spatial, in agreement with the shock-in-jet model of $\gamma$-ray emission.

claims.hypothesis: Is the flux-ratio variability due to micro/milli-lensing?
claims.experiment: Compare Einstein radii and drift timescales with the core size and observed variability timescales
claims.result: Core size (70-215 microarcsec) far exceeds micro-lensing Einstein radius (1.7 microarcsec); milli-lensing too slow for days-weeks, intra-day variability unexplained

evidence.quote: the intra-day variability detected in our ALMA observations cannot be explained with milli-lensing.

claims.hypothesis: Can a plasmon travelling in the jet explain the time and frequency dependence of the flux ratio?
claims.experiment: Fit conical and concave jet models with a plasmon using the 27-day lens delay
claims.result: Both reproduce the general trend; concave also reproduces the spectrum; 300 GHz May intra-day ratios need an extra flare
claims.finding: Concave jet with a narrow dense plasmon near the jet base is favored

evidence.quote: The fit to the May epochs is improved and the model can now reproduce the spectrum

claims.hypothesis: Where do the gamma-ray and submm flares originate?
claims.experiment: Compare model-derived injection time with Fermi-LAT flare
claims.result: Time lag at most a few days
claims.finding: Flares co-spatial near jet base, consistent with shock-in-jet

evidence.quote: the time-lag between the $\gamma$-ray and submm flares should not be larger than a few days

why_this_method.value: Flux ratio between lensed images is free of absolute calibration systematics and the lens delay allows detecting weak flares

evidence.loc: Comparison with mm/submm flaring activity in other AGN
evidence.quote: relative fluxes among images are free of absolute calibration effects, so very weak flares can be clearly detected

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Conical jet model rejected as unable to reproduce the steep spectrum; high-energy cutoff scenario also failed

evidence.loc: Effects of radiative and adiabatic cooling
evidence.quote: we conclude that our data are incompatible with the scenario of a conical jet

limitations_admitted.value: Many parameters with few data points prevent a statistically robust constraint of parameter space

evidence.quote: makes it difficult to constrain the parameter space in a statistically robust way
